here, the checklist's predictive validity is tested without direct manipulation by the non-expert panel."],"overturn_conditions":["The panel continues to perform reliably even when the checklist's cues are decorrelated from the outcome, suggesting the panel uses unstated external knowledge rather than the checklist's causal structure.","The objective outcome is fully determined by surface cues, making causal depth irrelevant and the distinction between compliance and structure meaningless."],"shared_structure":["Both involve a decision-making system relying on a proxy for an underlying latent variable.","Adversarial intervention (decorrelating proxy from latent) reveals whether the system uses the proxy as a direct cause or merely a surface indicator.","Performance collapse under intervention indicates proxy reliance; robustness indicates genuine structural understanding."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_002"],"transfer_claims":["The mechanism for detecting Goodhart's law (adversarial perturbation of the proxy) transfers to detecting mere checklist compliance.","If panel reliability survives the decorrelation of checklist cues from the outcome, the checklist has not become a Goodharted proxy."]},"claim":"A single evaluation can distinguish genuine reliability from mere checklist compliance by deploying adversarial items where the surface cues targeted by the checklist are decorrelated from the objective outcome; if panel performance survives this intervention, the checklist encodes causal structure rather than surface proxy.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The expert's internal model performs better than the checklist's frozen theory on the adversarial items, revealing that the checklist is a worse causal model.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The adversarial items are so far out-of-distribution that both the panel and the expert fail, making it impossible to distinguish checklist compliance from expert breakdown.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is explicitly designed as a non-causal surface heuristic, in which case compliance is the intended mechanism and the distinction is moot.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A checklist is a 'frozen theory' encoding a causal model. If non-experts merely track surface correlations, decorrelating those cues from the latent outcome on adversarial items will collapse panel accuracy. If the checklist captures causal structure, panel judgments will remain robust because the panel executes the underlying mechanism, not just the proxy. The evaluation distinguishes the two by measuring performance decay under cue-outcome decorrelation.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
